statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 71 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Weekend halt, hour eighteen: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, unresolved hawkish Warsh repricing with the 2-year near 4.35% against a semiconductor-led Friday decline
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August and the scheduled reopen falls about nine hours beyond the final slot of this window. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose about 11 to 12 basis points to roughly 4.32 to 4.35 percent, its highest in a month, against the 4.20 percent the Federal Reserve H.15 release records for 27 August; futures-implied odds of a September rate increase moved to roughly 57 to 59 percent from about 35 percent before the speech, with the decision meeting itself on 15 and 16 September, far beyond this window; and the dollar index rose about 0.5 percent. Single-name closes were verified directly this run rather than carried from intraday commentary: Nvidia closed down 4.57 percent at 217.55 and Marvell down 10.28 percent at 216.62 after a record data-centre quarter whose Google contribution was pushed out to fiscal 2029. Against that semiconductor leadership, Amazon rose about 4 percent and Microsoft, Alphabet, Apple and Meta all closed higher, so the carried-in signal is rotation rather than index-wide distribution. Gold fell roughly 3.2 percent to about $4,456 while WTI held near $83 and Brent near $88 to $89, extending weekly losses of about 4 percent, and a weekend-dated global briefing corroborates the same rates, dollar, gold and oil picture. Weekend research this run found no verified new market-relevant escalation: the Strait of Hormuz confrontation remains unresolved with transits far below pre-war levels, the 60-day US-Iran memorandum already lapsed in mid-August, and the transmission channel remains sanctions and shipping rather than a physical supply discontinuity. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 09:24 UTC, about five hours before this assessment, so it is stale under the inherited contract and is not used as confirmation; the assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources. Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots because a closed venue cannot generate the persistent no-retracement path the score measures; the mapped policy state is EA_ON throughout with no danger window. Friday's post-keynote repricing itself produced repeated retracements, which is why published Tail peaked at 22 and never reached the block threshold even at the height of the move, and why the front-end repricing is scored as a Stress input rather than a Tail amplifier. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read, the concentrated semiconductor decline, Broadcom results after the close on 2 September, and the 1 to 4 September stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP and the Beige Book, jobless claims and ISM Services, and August payrolls. Confidence runs 71 down to 65 across the window, in the solid band throughout, constrained only by the absence of a live price path rather than by thin or conflicting evidence. The first observable structure since Friday, including whether any gap retraces, whether pullbacks are shallow and whether the front end extends, will be scored on observed evidence in later cycles.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final six hours of Friday's cash session and the first eighteen hours of the weekend halt. The mode was event/whipsaw from 14:00 UTC as the Jackson Hole keynote hit the tape, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 16:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. Every hour of this window has a published assessment. The eighteen halt hours sit at a flat Tail of 5 with Stress in the low to mid twenties, and Confidence steps down from 88 to 72 purely as a function of tape age.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 32 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read with the 2-year near 4.32 to 4.35 percent and September hike odds around 57 to 59 percent, Friday's narrow semiconductor-led decline with Nvidia down 4.57 percent and Marvell down 10.28 percent, the roughly 3.2 percent drop in gold and 0.5 percent dollar gain that expressed the same repricing, the softer crude path near $83 WTI, Broadcom results after the close on 2 September, and the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP and the Beige Book, jobless claims and ISM Services, and August payrolls. Confidence decays from 71 to 65 across the window on tape age alone and stays in the solid band. The Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen falls about nine hours beyond the final slot, so the first observable structure since Friday, including whether any gap retraces, whether pullbacks are shallow and whether the front end extends Friday's move, is deliberately not anticipated with a score here and will be assessed on observed evidence in later cycles.
